title: ShopEase Mobile Shopping App - Product Requirements Document (Version 1 / MVP)
summary: ShopEase is our own fast, simple mobile shopping app for Android and iOS, built from a single shared codebase, where signed-in customers discover our clothing and accessories, buy them in a few taps with a card, and follow their orders. Version 1 sells to one country (Germany) in one currency (EUR) and one language (English). Prices shown include VAT, and the VAT amount is shown as a line on the order summary. Scope is the core shopping journey: email/password accounts with password reset, category browsing and keyword search, product detail with size/color variants and stock indication, cart, checkout with delivery address and delivery option (Standard EUR 4.90 in 3-5 working days, free from EUR 60; Express EUR 9.90 in 1-2 working days), Stripe card payment in test mode (PaymentIntents, no card data on our servers), order confirmation on screen and by email, order history with a single clear status per order, and email-only notifications. A web-based back-office with one admin role lets non-technical staff manage products, photos, prices and stock (manually and via CSV import), process orders, cancel orders, record refunds, and keep an audit trail. Guest checkout, social sign-in, push notifications, in-app returns, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, wishlists, discount codes and loyalty are out of scope for v1. Internally, orders follow pending_payment -> paid -> fulfilled -> delivered, plus cancelled and refunded. Customers see Placed, Processing, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled and Refunded. Stock is tracked per variant and reserved for 30 minutes from checkout start. Prices are stored as integer cents with currency code EUR. The target is a live release on Android and iOS around the end of December 2026, with Stripe live mode enabled by configuration only after the full test is passed. Success metrics in order: conversion rate, cart abandonment and checkout drop-off, repeat purchase rate, registered accounts. Analytics events are tracked with GDPR-compliant consent.

personas.name: Existing Customer (Quick Buyer)
personas.description: An existing customer of our clothing and accessories who wants a quicker, more convenient way to buy from us on their phone.
goals: Find a known product fast and pay in a few taps
Trust that stock shown is actually available
Receive a clear confirmation and receipt by email

personas.name: New Mobile Shopper
personas.description: A new shopper aged roughly 18-45 who discovers our brand and prefers shopping on mobile rather than a desktop website.
goals: Browse categories and search without needing any explanation
See photos, sizes, colors, price and stock status clearly
Create an account and check out with minimal friction

personas.name: Repeat Buyer
personas.description: A returning customer who wants to reorder, check past orders and see the status of each order.
goals: See order history with a clear status per order
Get email updates when an order ships, is delivered, cancelled or refunded
Find the returns policy and contact support easily

personas.name: Store Admin / Staff
personas.description: An internal, non-technical team member using the web back-office to add products, manage stock and prices, and process orders. One admin role with full access in v1; admin accounts are separate from shopper accounts.
goals: Load the initial catalog of a few hundred products via CSV and maintain it manually day to day
Update stock daily from a spreadsheet exported from the existing stock system and correct single items at any time
Move orders through statuses, cancel orders and record refunds with an audit trail

non_functional_requirements: Platforms: Android and iOS from the first release using a single shared codebase; Android is built and tested first, iOS follows in the same release. Minimum supported OS versions (for example Android 8.0+ and iOS 14+) to be confirmed at kickoff. Common phone sizes are supported in portrait; tablets and landscape are not required. The back-office is a responsive web app for current desktop browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).

Performance: on a mid-range phone over a 4G connection, cold app start to an interactive home screen within 3 seconds, category, search and product screens display content within 2 seconds at the 90th percentile, API responses under 500 ms at the 95th percentile for the catalog of a few hundred products. Images are served in optimized sizes and lazy-loaded.

Reliability: checkout and payment handling are idempotent; payment webhooks can be safely re-delivered; the expiry job releases stock for unpaid orders within 1 minute after the 30-minute window; stock can never become negative and concurrent checkouts cannot oversell the same variant.

Money handling: all prices and amounts are stored and calculated as integer minor units (cents) with ISO 4217 currency code EUR, never floats. Prices shown include VAT and the VAT amount is shown as a line on the order summary and confirmation email. Order lines copy product name and unit price at purchase time.

Payments and security: Stripe PaymentIntents in test mode; the server creates the intent, the app confirms it with the Stripe SDK, and a Stripe webhook marks the order paid; webhook signatures are verified. Card data never touches or is stored on our servers or logs. Switching to Stripe live mode requires only a configuration change of keys, and go-live happens only after the full test is passed.

Security: all traffic over TLS; passwords hashed with bcrypt or argon2; short-lived access tokens with refresh handling; server-side authorization so customers can only read and change their own cart, orders and data; admin endpoints restricted to admin accounts; rate limiting on sign-in and password reset; input validation on all endpoints; secrets kept out of source control; protection against common OWASP Top 10 risks; admin actions audit-logged.

Privacy and GDPR: store the minimum personal data; explicit consent before analytics tracking; account deletion supported from within the app; a privacy policy is accessible in the app; data retention for accounting records documented; personal data not written to logs; analytics data pseudonymous.

Accessibility: support system font scaling, minimum touch target of 44x44 points, sufficient color contrast (WCAG 2.1 AA), screen reader labels on interactive elements and images (VoiceOver and TalkBack), and errors conveyed by text and not color alone.

Localization: a single language (English), a single currency (EUR), a single country (Germany); text is kept in resource files to allow later localization; dates and numbers formatted for the Germany region.

Email: transactional emails (order confirmation, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refund confirmation, password reset) are branded, simple, sent within 1 minute of the trigger, and show order number and status where applicable.

Quality and testability: automated unit, API and integration tests cover the core journey (sign-up, browse, cart, checkout, payment, order status); OpenAPI documentation is kept current for the API; staging environment is available for acceptance testing with Stripe test mode.
Observability: server errors, failed payments, failed emails and failed imports are logged and monitored; crash reporting is enabled on the apps (respecting privacy rules).

Configuration: delivery prices and free-shipping threshold are configurable without an app release; the order reservation window is set to 30 minutes via server configuration; Stripe keys are environment configuration.
out_of_scope: Guest checkout (carts and orders belong to signed-in users only)
Social sign-in (Google, Apple); therefore Sign in with Apple is not required
Payment methods other than Stripe card payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal are deferred, with Apple Pay and Google Pay first)
In-app returns or return requests (customers contact support by email; refunds are handled manually in Stripe)
Automated refunds or partial refunds from within the back-office (recorded manually after issuing in Stripe)
PDF invoices (the confirmation email is the receipt; invoices are issued manually on request)
Multiple languages, multiple currencies or shipping outside Germany
Wishlists or favorites, discount codes, gift cards and loyalty programs
Product reviews and ratings, recommendations and personalization
Live integration with physical shop or stock systems (daily stock spreadsheet import only)
Multiple admin roles and permissions (one full-access admin role only)
Real-time order tracking with carrier integration or tracking numbers
Reserving stock when items are added to the cart (reserved only when checkout starts)
Live mode payments before the full test is passed
Social sharing, in-app chat support and customer support tooling
assumptions: Country is Germany, currency EUR, language English; the brief does not name the country and Germany was chosen by the customer.

Prices include VAT; the VAT amount on the order summary and in emails is calculated from the gross price using the applicable German rate (assumed 19% standard rate for clothing and accessories), configurable in one place; the exact rate and reduced-rate cases are to be confirmed with the customer's accountant.
The free-shipping threshold of EUR 60 is compared against the cart subtotal (items only, including VAT), before shipping, and Express is never free.

Internal order statuses are pending_payment, paid, fulfilled, delivered, cancelled and refunded. Processing is a customer-facing status for a paid order that an admin has started preparing; it is implemented as an admin-set marker on the paid order and not as an additional payment state.

Customer-facing mapping: Placed = pending_payment or paid (not yet picked up), Processing = paid and picked up by an admin, Shipped = fulfilled, Delivered = delivered, Cancelled = cancelled (including expired unpaid orders), Refunded = refunded.

Stock is tracked per variant (size and color). It is reserved for 30 minutes when checkout starts and permanently reduced when the order is paid; failed, cancelled or expired payments release the reservation. The customer's statement that stock is reduced when an order is paid is reconciled with the reservation model in this way.
Cancelling a paid order releases its stock and sends the Cancelled email, and the refund is issued manually in Stripe, after which the admin marks the order Refunded.
Orders can be cancelled by an admin only before they are fulfilled; after shipping, the return and refund policy applies.
Payment after an order has expired is a rare exception handled manually by the team (check stock, then fulfil or refund).
The first release uses Stripe test mode; moving to live mode is a configuration change made only after the full test is passed.

Product and stock data are loaded through CSV or spreadsheet import in the back-office using a documented template; the back-office is the single source of truth for what the app shows; the stock spreadsheet is imported once a day in the morning.

Admin accounts are created by the project team (no self-service admin sign-up), and the admin sign-in is secure with a password policy; second-factor authentication is desirable but not required for v1.
Minimum password length is 8 characters; password reset links are valid for 60 minutes and single use; these values can be changed at kickoff.
Email delivery uses a transactional email provider to be chosen by the development team; sending an email does not block a status change.
Content owners: product content (photos, descriptions) and customer support ownership after launch are internal staff roles still to be named by the customer.
Target launch is around the end of December 2026, about 3 months from the current date (30 September 2026), delivered in phases; no fixed budget figure yet.
Success metrics in priority order are conversion rate, cart abandonment and checkout drop-off, repeat purchase rate and registered accounts; downloads are secondary.

The returns policy (unworn items with tags within 30 days of delivery, full item price refund, return shipping paid by customer unless faulty) is shown as static text; the exact wording and support email address are supplied by the customer.
Legal pages such as privacy policy, terms and imprint required in Germany are supplied by the customer and displayed in the app as static pages.
